strengths: Well-motivated problem diagnosis: Convincingly shows that Prefix-Tuning's failure isn't due to inability to modify attention patterns (Figure 2), but rather an inherent input/prefix significance tradeoff clearly explained via Equation 4

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple datasets, models with different attention mechanisms (MHA/GQA), IID/OOD evaluation with Pareto analysis, varying data sizes, and practical alignment tasks (SFT, DPO, SimPO)
Clear mathematical framework: Progressive development from Equations 5-8 is logical and intuitive; effective decomposition of the attention output with prefixes
Consistent improvements over standard Prefix-Tuning: 29.4% average improvement demonstrates robustness across different settings
Unified framework for context-based methods: Section 5.2 provides useful perspective on design choices in PEFT methods
Good diagnostic analysis: Appendix B includes spectrum analysis, attention visualization, and CKA similarity studies that support the main claims
Well-written and clear presentation: Paper is generally well-structured with compelling motivation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is relatively incremental—primarily applies linearized attention techniques from [4] with straightforward modifications (fixed convex combination, kernel approximation, trainable matrices). Removing λ and N in practice further reduces elegance of the formulation

Incomplete theoretical understanding: While the paper identifies the tradeoff problem in Equation 4, it lacks rigorous explanation of why moving the prefix outside attention actually solves it. Equation 8 is still attention reweighting, just externalized. The fundamental mathematical constraints aren't analyzed

Arbitrary design choices with insufficient ablation: elu(x) kernel chosen as 'proof of concept' without exploration of alternatives; removing λ justified only by hand-waving about absorption into weights; no ablations comparing kernel approximation vs. exact attention; intermediate design in Eq. 9 never evaluated

Limited evaluation scope: Experiments only on few-shot settings (5-28 examples); models tested are relatively small (3B-7B); primarily classification tasks without generation, reasoning, or code; authors acknowledge no evaluation on abundant data; limited to supervised and alignment settings

Modest and inconsistent empirical improvements over LoRA: Claimed 8.1% average masks inconsistency (24.9% on GoEmotions, 2.9% on DBpedia, 5.6% on BigBench); no error bars or significance testing; results show PT+ is competitive rather than superior to LoRA

Missing critical ablations and sensitivity analysis: No ablation removing kernel approximation; no comparison of keeping prefix in attention head (Eq. 9) vs. external module (Eq. 8); no sensitivity to kernel function; no investigation of M dimensionality; no justification for each architectural removal

Fairness concerns in baseline comparisons: Unclear if hyperparameters equally tuned across methods; LoRA rank set to match parameter count but equivalence not established; no discussion of variance across random seeds; learning rate differences not addressed

Incomplete theoretical grounding: Why does external module M work better than internal biases? Connection between Figure 3 spectrum analysis and downstream performance not established; claims that larger CKA distance equals 'more expressive' are not validated

Narrow scope admits fundamental limitation: Authors acknowledge evaluating only in few-shot settings on small models and similar task types; 'modern LLMs' claims may be overstated; practical relevance for actual modern LLM applications unclear

strengths: Clear identification and mathematical exposition of Prefix-Tuning's fundamental tradeoff between prefix and input significance within attention heads (Eq. 4)
Empirical evidence refuting the prior assumption that Prefix-Tuning cannot modify attention patterns in deep models (Section 4.1, Figure 2)
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple models (LLaMA2, Qwen2.5), attention mechanisms (MHA, GQA), and evaluation regimes (IID/OOD, Pareto frontier analysis)
Unified framework conceptualizing the progression from ICL → Prompt-Tuning → Prefix-Tuning → PT+ with clear design trade-offs (Section 5.2)
Supplementary diagnostic experiments including spectrum analysis, CKA similarity, and attention visualization
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: the core contribution is incremental engineering (externalize prefix, apply kernel approximation, replace sums with trainable matrix M) heavily building on Chen et al. [4] without sufficient differentiation

Weak mathematical justification: key design choices lack rigor, including (1) the 'natural generalization' of replacing sums with M in Eq. 7, (2) arbitrary removal of φ(qi)ᵀN term, (3) hand-waved absorption of λ into weights via layer normalization

Questionable problem analysis: paper claims Prefix-Tuning fails due to inability to modify attention, then provides evidence it CAN, making the failure analysis disconnected from the proposed solution; moving the prefix outside attention reformulates rather than resolves the fundamental tradeoff

Narrow experimental scope severely limits claims: (1) only few-shot regime (1-6 examples per class), no moderate/high-data evaluation; (2) classification tasks only, despite original PT designed for generation; (3) missing baselines (P-Tuning v2, Prompt Tuning variants); (4) no statistical significance testing despite close margins

Inconsistent and modest improvements over LoRA across datasets (9.0% on GoEmotions, 2.6% on DBpedia, 3.8% on BigBench), with no significance testing or validation that improvements are real rather than noise

Critical ablation studies entirely missing: (1) no comparison of keeping prefix in attention head but using trainable M (Eq. 9); (2) no ablation on feature map choice despite ELU being acknowledged as suboptimal; (3) no analysis of matrix M dimensionality sensitivity; (4) authors acknowledge 'design has yet to be thoroughly ablated'

Confusing interpretation of diagnostic experiments: Table 3 shows PT+ has larger CKA distance (0.9432) than LoRA (0.9978), but claim of 'stronger expressive capacity' from larger representation shifts is not clearly justified; Table 4 shows longer prefixes increase changes but doesn't explain why PT fails or PT+ succeeds
Missing efficiency analysis despite 'parameter-efficient' framing: no memory usage, training time, FLOPs, or inference overhead comparison; unclear how many parameters M introduces
Unvalidated theoretical claim in Remark 1: suggests ReLU(Wx+b) enables expressivity matching full fine-tuning but only ELU is tested experimentally

Presentation and clarity issues: (1) title 'Attention Independent Prefix Data' is misleading—method still uses attention; (2) Eq. 8 operation (how is addition implemented?) not clearly explained; (3) notation inconsistently tracked (λ absorbed without clear documentation)

strengths: Novel reframing of PT's failure: Identifies input/prefix significance tradeoff (Eq. 4) rather than inability to alter attention patterns, supported by empirical evidence (Figure 2)
Clear mathematical progression: Well-motivated construction from standard PT through kernel approximation to final PT+ architecture (Equations 3-8)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple datasets (4), models (2 architectures with different attention mechanisms), tasks (few-shot classification + alignment), and diagnostic analyses (attention visualization, CKA, spectrum analysis)
Consistent improvements over baseline: Substantial gains over standard PT (29.4% average improvement) across multiple benchmarks and settings
Valuable conceptual framework: Section 5.2 provides unified perspective on context-based PEFT design space, facilitating future research
Strong diagnostic support: Eigenvalue spectrum analysis (Figure 3) and CKA similarity (Table 3) provide evidence for expressivity claims
Practical relevance: Addresses real problem of PT's poor performance on modern LLMs with a relatively simple solution
weaknesses: Inconsistent and mixed results vs. LoRA: While PT+ shows strong improvements on some tasks (GoEmotions: +9-10.5%, BigBench Qwen: +15.2%), gains are marginal on others (DBpedia LLaMA2: +2.6%, BigBench LLaMA2: +3.8%), making the 8.1% average improvement claim somewhat selective

Insufficient ablation studies: Missing critical ablations isolating Choice 1 (moving prefix out) from Choice 2 (kernel approximation), no ablation on matrix M dimensionality, contradicting thoroughness claims

Weak feature map justification: ELU chosen as 'easiest to implement' and 'proof of concept'—more expressive alternatives like ϕ_W(x) = ReLU(Wx+b) mentioned but not tested, leaving performance gains unexplored
Suspicious baseline performance: Standard PT achieving only 5.6% on GoEmotions (LLaMA2) suggests potential undertunning, which inflates relative improvement claims

Limited evaluation scope: Primarily few-shot settings with 1-5 examples; mostly classification tasks; alignment experiments (Section 6.5) brief and single-model; no broader evaluation on QA, summarization, instruction-following

Theoretical gaps: No analysis of kernel approximation error, connection between eigenvalue decay and downstream performance assumed rather than proven, claim in Remark 1 about matching full fine-tuning expressivity unsupported
Incomplete parameter accounting: Exact parameter counts for PT+ vs LoRA never provided despite claiming 'approximate match' with r=64
Missing design ablations: No systematic exploration of M dimensionality or other architectural choices; authors acknowledge limited exploration in Appendix D limitations section

strengths: Clear and insightful diagnosis of Prefix-Tuning's failure through the prefix-input contribution tradeoff analysis (Eq. 3), with solid empirical verification that PT can modify attention patterns in deep models

Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning diagnostic (few-shot) and large-scale (SFT, DPO, math reasoning) settings with thoughtful IID/OOD generalization analysis via Pareto plots and testing across different attention mechanisms (MHA/GQA)
Substantial empirical improvements on several benchmarks (e.g., 71.2% vs 67.4% on BigBench, 38.6% vs 23.9% improvement on Minerva-Math), with consistent gains on preference alignment tasks
Principled mathematical derivation from Eq. 2→7 clearly motivating design choices, supported by spectrum analysis (Fig. 3) demonstrating increased expressivity of PMT's bias contributions
Efficiency analysis showing competitive throughput and latency, with reasonable parameter efficiency compared to LoRA
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is incremental refinement of Chen et al. (2024)—replacing a bias term with trainable matrix M. Kernel approximations are standard; the modification lacks fundamental innovation

Insufficient ablation studies: Critical design choices lack empirical validation—simplifications in Eq. 6→7 (removing λ and φ(qᵢ)ᵀN) justified only informally; limited exploration of feature map choices (only ELU vs GELU); no ablation on M dimensionality

Unjustified mathematical steps: Jump from Eq. 5 (exact sums) to Eq. 6 (trainable M) lacks analysis of approximation quality or information loss. Claim that layer norm 'absorbs' λ needs rigorous justification. ELU kernel choice problematic (negative outputs violate kernel positivity)

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Missing comparisons to recent context-based methods (P-Tuning v2, DePT, ADePT) mentioned in related work; LoRA+ relegated to single table; limits assessment of PMT's position in PEFT landscape

Mixed empirical results with weak statistical rigor: Improvements over LoRA often modest (1-3 points); GoEmotions gains marginal; no significance testing or confidence intervals despite 5-run averaging; some differences likely not statistically significant

Limited experimental scale: Only 3B-7B models tested; claim these are 'proxies for larger architectures' is unvalidated. For 2026 venue standards, 70B+ evaluation expected. Limited evaluation in abundant-data regimes acknowledged in Appendix E

Unclear practical advantage and missing critical analysis: No characterization of when PMT substantially outperforms alternatives; missing empirical case for switching from established LoRA; CKA analysis interpretation unclear (PMT 0.9432 vs LoRA 0.9978 similarity to base)

Reproducibility and design limitation concerns: Code not released; feature map choices artificially constrained (learnable maps dismissed without empirical validation in Remark 1); incomplete justification for design decisions limits future improvements

Overstated claims: '8.1% improvement over LoRA' cherry-picked from few-shot setting; title 'modernizing' Prefix-Tuning suggests broader impact than incremental refinement; 'proof of concept' framing doesn't justify the positioning

strengths: Clear problem identification: Section 4.2 articulates a concrete tradeoff between prefix and input contribution within softmax normalization through formal analysis (Equation 3)
Comprehensive experimental protocol: Balanced IID/OOD evaluation with Pareto plots, multiple architectures (MHA, GQA), diverse benchmarks, and multiple models
Solid diagnostic analysis: Eigenvalue decay (Figure 3) and CKA similarity (Table 9) provide mechanistic insights into representation changes
Methodologically rigorous evaluation setup: Proper experimental design with clear protocols across diagnostic and large-scale settings
Addresses a real limitation: Prefix-Tuning's poor performance on modern LLMs is well-motivated and the proposed decoupling is intuitive
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core mechanism (φ(q)^T M approximation) directly applies existing linearized attention techniques; extension to externalize prefix is straightforward modification of Chen et al. (2024)

Weak theoretical foundation: Key design choices lack rigorous justification—sim approximation unvalidated, removal of regularization term unjustified, arbitrary transitions between equations (e.g., Eq. 5→6)

Marginal empirical improvements with no statistical validation: Improvements over LoRA range from 2.6% (DBpedia) to 8% (GoEmotions) with high task variance; no significance tests, confidence intervals, or error bars despite only 5 trials

Limited experimental scale: Evaluation restricted to 3B-7B models; 70B+ model evaluation acknowledged as infeasible due to computational constraints, weakening claims about 'modern LLMs'; primarily classification tasks, no language modeling
Missing critical ablations: No isolation of kernel approximation component, no analysis of learned M structure, no alternative parameterization comparisons, no hyperparameter sensitivity analysis

Incomplete analysis of Prefix-Tuning's failure: Section 4.1 claims PT modifies attention patterns, contradicting Petrov et al.; connection between α-tradeoff (Section 4.2) and poor performance lacks formal validation
Self-acknowledged as incomplete: Authors describe work as 'primarily a proof of concept' with design elements explicitly deferred to future work (learnable kernels, sophisticated feature maps)
Questionable baseline comparisons: PT uses m=32 while LoRA uses r=64; unclear if m=32 was thoroughly tuned for fair comparison
Insufficient engagement with related work: Limited integration of concurrent work (Meyer et al. 2025); unclear why LoRA avoids the alleged prefix-input tradeoff despite modifying attention
Marginal efficiency gains: Tables 5-6 show throughput/latency improvements are inconsistent and often comparable to Prefix-Tuning baseline

strengths: Clear problem diagnosis: The paper provides excellent mathematical insight into why Prefix-Tuning fails on modern LLMs, moving beyond prior work by formalizing the α-weighted tradeoff between input and prefix contributions (Equation 3, Section 4.2)

Comprehensive experimental validation: Well-structured diagnostic experiments with IID/OOD evaluation across multiple datasets, large-scale experiments on preference alignment and math reasoning, plus verification experiments (spectrum analysis, attention visualization, CKA similarity)

Strong reproducibility and scientific practices: Detailed implementation details, hyperparameter specifications, multiple independent runs, careful parameter reporting, honest discussion of limitations, and transparent acknowledgment of the work as a proof-of-concept

Practical impact and revived method: Successfully revives Prefix-Tuning (29.4% improvement over vanilla PT) to competitive performance with LoRA (8.1% average improvement) across diverse benchmarks and model architectures
Unified framework contribution: Section 5.3 provides a useful unified view of design choices in context-based PEFT methods that can guide future work
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core technique builds on Chen et al. (2024)'s linearized attention approach, with the main contribution being problem identification rather than novel methodology. Authors acknowledge the approach is 'naive' and admit limited architectural exploration

Insufficient theoretical justification: Key design choices lack rigorous justification—the kernel approximation quality is assumed not validated, the transition to trainable matrix M from Equation 5→6 is heuristic, and replacing adaptive softmax with fixed λ is not well motivated

Incomplete ablations: Feature map φ(·) only briefly explored (2 activations); trainable feature maps explicitly left for future work; no systematic study of matrix M dimensionality; missing ablations on architecture necessity

Experimental limitations: (1) Evaluations limited to 3B-7B models despite claims about 'modern LLMs'—no validation on 70B+ models; (2) Only few-shot/application settings; (3) Modest improvements over LoRA (8.1%) are good but not transformative; (4) Missing comparisons with recent methods (DePT, ADePT, GaLore) mentioned in related work

Overstated claims and framing issues: Title and abstract suggest stronger contributions than results support; on some benchmarks both PMT and PT significantly underperform full fine-tuning; the 'memory perspective' (Remark 2) feels post-hoc; CKA analysis (Table 9) shows PMT deviates more from base model than LoRA but implications unclear

Heuristic design decisions: Fixed λ replacing adaptive normalization, kernel approximation validity not analyzed, matrix M initialization/design not explored, and overall approach self-described as 'proof of concept' rather than complete solution
